newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Occidental loses $3.3 mln/day over field shut-in.
newsitem.headline: Occidental loses $3.3 mln/day over field shut-in.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp said it was losing $3.3 million for every day production was shut-in at the Cano Limon oil field it operates in northeast Colombia.
Output was halted early Monday after a series of back-to-back rebel attacks and a damaging landslide ruptured the main pipeline that transports crude to the Caribbean coast port of Covenas.

Occidental has also declared force majeure in the field, for the second time in three weeks -- a situation which could last for a week, a spokesman told Reuters. He added that despite the problems caused by halting production he did not think any of the 130 wells in the field would be damaged.
"There's alaways a risk of damage to wells in a situation like this but I don't think there will be any damage in this case," the spokesman said.

He was unable to comment on the possibility of declaring force majeure on crude exports since the decision depends largely on state-run oil company Ecopetrol which operates the lifting terminal at Covenas.
